commits: b3070cd3 Drafts merge a save another save beat, instead of refusing or replaying it
ef842c45 Gen composer: every take files on the draft as the server holds it
acea9b9d Rig: renders show in Takes, Send to Rig works while open, ⌘Z stays home
1b710981 A deleted project never strands the drafts and originals that pointed at it
a3548ea7 One regression spec for a draft edited in several places at once
a811fa67 Drafts: a lost reply is checked, not merged again; a merge is a save the server takes
design:
Whole branch (fix/rig-leave-save, 6 commits on a30977f3). All of it runs against the ENGINE_MOCK dev server; nothing is billed.

1. Merging instead of refusing (b3070cd3, extended in a811fa67). One project draft has several editors: the Rig, the Studio stages (use-draft-editor), Edit & Sound (draft-editor), Marketing, the Gen composer, and other tabs. Each editor keeps `base`, the draft exactly as the server last held it. The server keeps its revision check (saveDraft) and still answers a stale revision with 409 code "revision_conflict" (DraftConflictError). The editor then reads the latest version, merges the edits it made since `base` into it, and saves at that revision, at most MERGE_TRIES times.
- lib/workbench/merge.ts, merge3(base, mine, theirs), generic over JSON. Objects merge key by key. A key one side deleted goes only if the other side left it unchanged. Lists of records merge by id, or by genId/jobId/assetId where those are unique. New in a811fa67: lists keyed by a number `frame` or `page` are kept in numeric order. Order is mine's, unless only theirs moved records. A record deleted on one side and changed on the other is kept. No id appears twice. Lists of distinct single-token strings (links, refs, references) merge as sets.
- Also new in a811fa67: other string lists and records without an identity merge as sequences, with Myers diff plus diff3. Stretches only one side changed are kept. When both sides insert at the same place, both insertions stay, mine's first. When one side only added items, those additions join the other side's version. When both sides rewrote the same stretch, mine stands, or theirs if mine only deleted it. Text with several lines merges line by line the same way. Keys are written as own properties, so `__proto__` is kept as data. An optional `ancestors` map (records an undo put back) supplies a base for a record both sides hold but base lacks.
- lib/workbench/draft-merge.ts (new), mergeDraft. It runs merge3, then two project-level steps:
  - A merge never leaves a link to a dropped node. A media input one side removed only because nothing else used it is restored if the other side wired it in. Any other link to a node that is gone is removed, including activeInput.
  - If a list or text grew beyond both sides' versions, the result is checked against saveSchema, and anything too_big is fitted the way its stage fits it: takes and plates keep the newest, pending keeps the latest five, other lists keep what the saved side had first and then this side's additions, and text past its limit is this side's.
  - rebaseProject lays edits made while a save was out over the saved result, through the same merge.

2. A save whose reply was lost is checked, never guessed at (a811fa67). The server adds a table, workbench_draft_writes: one row per owner, draft and writer, holding seq, revision (or NULL) and updated_at, pruned after 30 days. A PUT may carry `write: {writer, seq}`. saveDraft refuses a tag whose seq is at or below the one recorded, as revision_conflict, and records a tag that lands. The new POST action `check-write` on /api/workbench/projects says whether a tagged save landed (and its revision). A save that has not landed is fenced in the same transaction, so it can never land late. The response also returns the draft as it is now. These are extensions of the existing route and lib; nothing is replaced.
- In the client (draft-request.ts), a DraftWriter is `{id, seq, unconfirmed}`. writeMergedDraft tags every PUT. When a reply is unknown, it asks the server:
  - Landed: it returns the latest version. Nothing is sent again, so a later rewrite, rename or delete by another window stands.
  - Not landed: it merges and sends.
  - The server cannot be asked: the write stays unconfirmed on the writer, and the next call settles it first. If it landed, edits since are merged from what it carried, so an undo or a cleared field is saved as such.
- writeDraft with a writer uses the same check. Without a writer it keeps the old reconcile heuristic, which the other suites still use.
- use-draft-editor, draft-editor, the Rig (one writer per draft) and the composer's saveOnLatest all pass writers. use-draft-editor no longer treats "back to base" as saved while a write is unconfirmed.

3. What two windows make at once is made once. New module lib/workbench/stable-id.ts, stableId(prefix, ...parts), a 64-bit hash. These now take stable ids:
- the direction op in shotPatch, keyed by node;
- sound lanes, keyed by role, with a fallback if that id is taken;
- places and cast entries from an agent run (by job and name) or from the beat sheet;
- beat sheets from a breakdown (by job or source, and position);
- Marketing variants, keyed by the node they are bound to;
- buildFromBoards shots and their frame inputs.

4. Rig and team canvas.
- Server side: saveDraft now applies a field-level diff of each save's nodes to the production's team canvas, when that canvas exists and inside the same transaction. Every editor's node edits reach the canvas, so reopening the Rig never reverts them.
- Patch model: TeamPatch gains `fields` (only the changed keys are written onto the canvas node, or onto the removed copy, which comes back) and `made` (a new node or an undo restore joins only if the canvas does not already hold that node). A whole-node PATCH with neither keeps its old overwrite meaning.
- Client side: the Rig's PATCH and live writes are field-level too, so a merge never puts a stale prompt over a teammate's.
- RigProvider:
  - ⌘Z acts only when the shell is on the draft's project.
  - Dirty drafts of a project the person leaves are parked and saved with backoff. Returning to that project takes the parked draft back.
  - Save state resets on a switch.
  - A refusal keeps the edits and says so instead of reloading.
  - Restored shots carry ancestors.
- RigInspector: the Name field follows a merged-in rename.
- Earlier commits on the branch (acea9b9d): a take shows in Takes when accepted and when it lands, Send to Rig works while the Rig is open, and ⌘Z refuses to act in another project.

5. Gen composer (ef842c45, extended in a811fa67). Each take files its shot on the draft as the server holds it (saveOnLatest). A take whose paid request is unconfirmed is remembered in localStorage, per project, together with its quote key and its place in the batch.
- The next Generate with the same settings (after leaving Gen or a reload) reuses the same shot and claimed request and continues from that take, so a two-take ask costs two takes.
- A connected take is remembered before its submit and read back on the next Generate. It is never submitted twice.
- Sound recovery keys are per lane plus settings, so a new prompt at a new price is a new request. The lane is looked up again on every attempt.
- Connected takes are followed through a store shared by composer instances, so takes submitted after Gen closed are followed and filed.

6. A deleted project no longer strands its drafts (1b710981). Drafts linked to it keep saving, and its library filings are archived.

Every reproduced break was a real defect. One artifact: the canvas-undo-2 spec expected a second successful PUT, but after the dangling wire is removed the merged draft equals the server's version, so nothing needs to be sent. The folded test checks the substance instead: no link to nothing, and the grade takes Second. The probes that were not breaks (canvas-undo-8, composer-money-7, the canvas-undo-3 control) passed before and after. composer-money-3 was folded in as coverage for the composer's checked saves. docs/production-workbench.md is updated to match.
findings_fixed: A save whose reply was lost was merged again over a later save from another window. The Cast rewrite and delete, the Rig's + Add shot then delete, and the Rig rename (Alpha then Bravo) all lost the later edit. Fix: saves carry writer tags, and POST check-write answers whether a lost save landed and fences it if not. A save that landed is never sent again (draft-request.ts, records.ts).

An undo, a cleared field or ⌘Z made while a save was unconfirmed was lost when the save was retried from the old base (merge-algebra r1-4 and r1-5). Fix: the unconfirmed write stays on the writer and is settled first; edits made since are merged from what it carried. use-draft-editor no longer treats 'equal to base' as saved while a write is unconfirmed.
Two windows each writing a shot's first direction note gave the shot two direction ops, and one note was invisible. Fix: shotPatch creates the direction op with a stable id per node.

Merging two valid saves could produce a draft the server refused (400): references above 6, plates above 30, takes above 20, pending above 5, hooks above 12. The stage then stopped saving, and the Rig reloaded and dropped its edits. Fix: draft-merge.ts fits any list that grew past its limit the way its stage does, hooks merge as a sequence, and the Rig keeps its edits instead of reloading.

Two Environment tabs taking one agent run put every place in the draft twice. The same pattern existed for the Cast agent take, beat sheets, the 'from beats' buttons, Marketing variant binding and building shots from storyboards. Fix: each takes a stable id derived from its source (stable-id.ts).

A merge could keep a link to a node the merge dropped: a grade was left with an input nobody could see, and a plate that theirs had wired was lost. Fix: mergeDraft restores media inputs the other side wired in and removes every other dangling link.

Switching project while the Rig's save was out meant the merged edit never reached the team canvas, and reopening reverted the other window's edit. Fix: each draft save publishes a field-level diff of its nodes to the production's canvas, on the server.

The Rig reopening put the canvas's older version of a shot over a draft edit made elsewhere (a pre-existing join problem). Fix: the same server-side publish on every draft save, so the canvas is never older than the draft.

A merge published whole stale shots to the team canvas, overwriting a teammate's edit to fields the Rig never touched. Fix: TeamPatch now carries `fields` and `made`; the Rig's PATCH and live writes, and the server's apply, write only the fields an edit changed.

⌘Z of a deleted shot wrote its old snapshot over another window's edit that a merge had brought back. Fix: restored shots carry ancestors into merge3, and on the canvas a `made` node never overwrites a live one.

⌘Z pressed while the next project was still loading said the shot was back, then dropped the restore and used up the undo entry. Fix: the undo checks the shell's current project, and unsaved edits to a project being left are parked and saved instead of being dropped.

An unconfirmed save followed by a project switch dropped the edits, and A's error kept showing in B (pre-existing on main). Fix: the project being left is parked and retried with backoff until saved, and the save state resets on the switch.

Gen sound takes shared the lane's recovery key, so a new prompt at a new price replayed an old unconfirmed request with no price gate. Fix: the recovery key covers the lane plus the settings of the take.

A Gen take whose paid reply was lost was paid for again after leaving Gen or reloading. Fix: the unconfirmed take is remembered in localStorage per project, and the next Generate with the same settings reuses its shot and claimed request.
Recovering take 2 of a two-take batch also bought a new third take. Fix: the batch resumes from the take that failed.

A connected take whose submit reply was lost was quoted and submitted again on the next Generate. Fix: the take is remembered before submitting and read back first. A take the account accepted is followed, never submitted again.
Connected takes submitted after the person left Gen were never followed or filed. Fix: a follow store shared by composer instances in the same page, written as each take is submitted.
Gen created a second sound lane when Edit & Sound made one while Gen's save was out. Fix: the lane is looked up again on every attempt, and lanes have stable ids.
The Inspector's Name field kept a stale name after a merged-in rename, and typing saved the old name back. Fix: the field follows the shot's name.

Keyframes, records without an id and multi-line text dropped the other side's change (mine won outright). Fix: they now merge as diff3 sequences or line by line; keyframes are keyed by frame and script pages by page, in order.
A record key named __proto__ vanished in a merge (the prototype setter). Fix: merged keys are written as own properties.

pr_title: Drafts: merge a save another save beat, check lost replies on the server, make each thing once
pr_body:
## Summary

One project draft has several editors at once: the Rig, the Studio stages, Edit & Sound, Marketing, the Gen composer, and other tabs. The save is revision-checked, so whichever save landed second used to be refused, and that editor stopped saving or reloaded and dropped its edits. This branch merges instead, and closes every break that three review rounds reproduced.

- **Merging.** Each editor keeps the draft as the server last held it (`base`). When the server answers a stale revision with 409 `revision_conflict`, the editor reads the latest version and saves `mergeDraft(base, mine, latest)` (`lib/workbench/merge.ts`, `lib/workbench/draft-merge.ts`).
  - Objects merge key by key.
  - Lists of records merge by id (keyframes by frame, script pages by page).
  - Lists of ids merge as sets.
  - Other lists and multi-line text merge stretch by stretch (diff3).
  - A record deleted on one side and changed on the other is kept.
  - A shot restored by ⌘Z merges from what it was when deleted.
  - The result is always a save the server accepts: no link points at a dropped node, and a list that grew past its limit is fitted the way its stage fits it.
- **Lost replies are checked, never guessed.** Each save carries `{writer, seq}`, recorded in a new `workbench_draft_writes` table. `POST /api/workbench/projects {action: "check-write"}` says whether a save landed and fences it if it did not. A save that landed is never sent again over what another window built on it. A save left unconfirmed is settled before the next one, so an undo made meanwhile is saved as an undo. The revision check and the `revision_conflict` code are unchanged.
- **One of each.** A shot's first direction note, sound lanes, places and cast from an agent run or the beat sheet, beat sheets, Marketing variants and shots built from storyboards take stable ids from their source (`lib/workbench/stable-id.ts`). Two windows making the same thing make it once.
- **Team canvas.**
  - Each draft save carries its node edits to the production's canvas, field by field, whichever editor made them.
  - The Rig's own canvas edits send only the fields they changed.
  - A node an edit made, or an undo put back, joins the canvas only if it is not already there.
- **Rig.**
  - ⌘Z acts only on the project the shell is on.
  - Edits to a project the person leaves unsaved keep being saved.
  - A refused save keeps its edits instead of reloading.
  - The Inspector's Name follows a rename merged in from another window.
  - Renders show in Takes, and Send to Rig works while the Rig is open.
- **Gen composer.**
  - Every take files its shot on the draft as the server holds it.
  - A take left unconfirmed is taken up again, with its shot and its claimed request, after leaving Gen or reloading, and the batch resumes from it. No take is paid for twice.
  - Sound takes recover per lane and settings, so a new prompt at a new price is a new request.
  - A connected take whose submit reply was lost is read back first, never submitted twice.
  - Takes submitted after Gen closed are still followed and filed.
- **Deleted projects.** A draft whose project was deleted still saves, and the project's library filings are archived.

## Noticed, not changed here
- In a live Liveblocks room with teammates present, joining still takes the room's nodes over draft edits made outside the Rig. The server cannot write to a live room. Saved mode, which is what runs without a Liveblocks key, is fixed.
- `lib/storage.ts` `openUploadStream` throws an uncaught AbortError when a local-disk upload read is aborted. It only affects the local dev storage path, and it is filed as a separate task.

## Test plan
- [x] Unit project: 2067 passed, 3 skipped. `tests/unit/draft-merge.spec.ts`, `draftRequest.spec.ts`, `workbenchRecords.spec.ts` and `teamCanvas.spec.ts` include the folded break scenarios.
- [x] `tests/suites-draft-merge-workbench.spec.ts` (1440×900, ENGINE_MOCK): 41 passed. That is the 14 original tests plus 28 folded ones: 27 reproduced browser breaks and one composer probe kept as coverage.
- [x] Related browser specs (team canvas, stage switch, Cast, Environment, Beats, Rig, Edit & Sound, Gen, the composer, Marketing, Storyboards): 37 passed, 4 skipped.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` and eslint on the changed files: clean.
